reportOnlyUntil: APPLY ONLY AFTER #2041 is merged AND deployed AND the Heavy Metal rows are ingested (metal-universe-heavy-metal:N exists) — the REPORT will show refused/occupied until then. NO APPLY IS AUTHORIZED BY THIS PR.
finding: PR #2041 registers `metal-universe-heavy-metal` as a non-collapsing setKey (parent `metal-universe`); until it merges and deploys, normalizeSetKey collapses that key to `metal-universe`, so the 1996 Fleer Metal Universe "Heavy Metal" 10-card named insert never minted its own card_catalog rows. #2041's PR comments (2026-09-11) measured all ten Heavy Metal numbers against prod card_catalog and found the absorption hits FIVE numbers, 18 rows total: #1 Albert Belle (3 rows), #2 Barry Bonds (6 rows), #6 Mike Piazza (5 rows), #8 Frank Thomas (2 rows), #10 Matt Williams (2 rows). #3, #4, #5, #7, #9 are clean. By source: 17 baseballcardpedia-graded + 1 ingest-auto-seed. Re-measured by this repair 2026-09-12 by point-read: identical 18-row population, identical single sale (on hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:ssp:no-auto, visible only on hobbyiqCardId — byCardId=0, byHobbyiqCardId=1, byEither=1).
rulings: THE 5 BASE-CARD PARENTS AT THESE ADDRESSES ARE CORRECT AND ARE NOT IN THIS FILE. Point-read 2026-09-12 of all 5 plain (`:base:no-auto`, no grade tier) rows at 1996 metal-universe #1/#2/#6/#8/#10: every one is the CHECKLIST-BACKED base player (Roberto Alomar, Brady Anderson, Mike Mussina, Rafael Palmeiro, B.J. Surhoff respectively; source `baseballcardpedia-ladders-2026-09-02`, the checklist authority). These are real, correctly-named base cards and must never move or be touched by this repair — the absorption is NOT that the base card itself is misnamed, it is that 17 GRADED CHILDREN of these correct base parents carry the wrong (Heavy Metal) playerName, and 1 separate ungraded SSP-parallel row was minted under the wrong parent's number.

NO ENTRIES FOR GRADED CHILDREN. 17 of the 18 absorbed rows are graded children (id shape `${parentSlug}:${tier}`, e.g. `hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:base:no-auto:psa-9`, `parentSlug: hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:base:no-auto`) of the CORRECT base parent, each individually mislabelled with the Heavy Metal player's name instead of the base player's. moveCatalogRow/retireCatalogRow carry (retire) children with their parent on a card-level move, and a child given its OWN reslug entry onto a plain card address is refused outright ("a graded child cannot move onto a card address") — PR #2041's own comment names this as the 53-failure mode on REPORT run 34356734615. Since the base parent itself is correct and stays put, these 17 children have no card-level move to follow: fixing them is a FIELD REPAIR (playerName/displayName/searchTokens on the existing graded child, or a graded-child-to-graded-child reslug once the Heavy Metal card address exists) that is out of scope for a catalog ADDRESS relocation list, and is left to whoever runs the post-ingest repair PR #2041 asks for. A reslug of one onto a plain card address would also DROP THE GRADE (buildIncoming refuses a gradeTier-present id landing on a gradeTier-absent slug), so no such entry is written here under any framing.

THE ONE UNGRADED ROW IS THE ONLY ENTRY. `hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:ssp:no-auto` (source ingest-auto-seed) is a plain card-level row, not a graded child, and its own `cardNumber`/`playerName` (2, Barry Bonds) are the Heavy Metal card, mis-set-keyed onto `metal-universe` by the same normalizeSetKey collapse #2041 fixes on the ingest path. This is the one row in the 18 that is both (a) card-level, so moveCatalogRow's card-vs-card guard applies cleanly, and (b) actually a Heavy Metal identity rather than a base parent that happens to have a bad child. It reslugs to `hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe-heavy-metal:2:ssp:no-auto`.

keepSales: true — THE ONE SALE STAYS AT THE OLD SLUG. Exactly one sale rests on the SSP row being reslugged here (byCardId=0, byHobbyiqCardId=1, byEither=1 — the same cardId/hobbyiqCardId disagreement #2041's comments flagged for the Finest pool repoint list). Per CF-A-DISENTANGLEMENT-DOES-NOT-CARRY-THE-OTHER-CARD'S-SALES this reslug separates the Heavy Metal SSP card from the base-set address it was wrongly filed under; the sale is a genuine Heavy Metal Bonds sale and belongs at the new address once it exists, but this list does not carry it there itself — the rematch re-derives hobbyiqCardId/cardId against the genuine year/number/parallel identity after ingest. (Recorded for completeness: `keepSales` is nearly a no-op on a same-address-family reslug where the destination has never existed before; it is set anyway so a re-run after #2041 ships behaves identically whether or not the destination has since accumulated its own sales.)

APPLY ONLY AFTER #2041 SHIPS AND THE HEAVY METAL CHECKLIST INGESTS — CORRECTED FROM 'REFUSED/OCCUPIED'. The one destination in this file (`hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe-heavy-metal:2:ssp:no-auto`) does not exist yet: normalizeSetKey still collapses `metal-universe-heavy-metal` to `metal-universe` on the INGEST path until #2041 merges and deploys, and the parent Heavy Metal card_catalog rows are only minted once the Heavy Metal checklist ingest runs (10 rows, per #2041's comment). A REPORT run against this file TODAY was measured 2026-09-12 and does NOT show refused/occupied as originally expected: normalizeSetKey's collapse only applies at ingest time, not to this lane's literal point-read of the destination slug, and no row exists there to refuse onto — moveCatalogRow's `rowAt` finds nothing and the report predicts a clean RESLUG (`entries in scope 1, RESLUGGED (moved) 1, sales LEFT BEHIND 1`). THAT IS THE HAZARD, NOT A SAFETY NET: an APPLY run today would silently mint an orphaned, un-normalized `metal-universe-heavy-metal:2:ssp:no-auto` row before the key is registered and before the Heavy Metal checklist exists to reconcile against it — worse than a refusal, because nothing stops the write. The gate is therefore a PROCESS gate, not a mechanical one: this file must not be run with BACKFILL_APPLY=true until #2041 is merged, deployed, and the 10-row Heavy Metal checklist ingest has landed at metal-universe-heavy-metal:1 through :10. This file is committed now, per the #2041 follow-up comment's instruction to whoever writes the post-ingest fold list, so the list exists and is reviewed before it is needed — but the report's own numbers are not the enforcement mechanism here; the human process gate is.
